title: Crash help: the server has to be signed in first

must_contain.why: a test for the new entry

instruction:
Add ONE new entry to the PATTERNS list in core/diagnose.py, in the same 5-part form as the
others: (key, regex, title, fix, link).

- key: "needs_signin"
- where in the list: as the FIRST entry of PATTERNS (before "port_taken")
- the regex (case is ignored) must match these console lines: 'LogBRAuthSubsystem: Error: Authentication failed on dedicated server. Exiting now.' and '[200] Account Failed (6): "E_INVALID_TOKEN"' and 'No auth token could be found.'
- title (exactly): "The game's server has to be signed in first"
- fix (exactly, split over lines like the other entries so no line is over 118 characters): "This game only runs a server that is linked to an account with the game's maker. Follow the game's own server guide to get a server token (or to sign the server in), then start it again."
- link: None

Then add assertions at the END of test_explain_patterns_and_exit_codes in tests/test_engine.py (same style,
8 spaces of indentation):
        for line in ("LogBRAuthSubsystem: Error: Authentication failed on dedicated server. Exiting now.",
                     '[00:00:04]: [200] Account Failed (6): "E_INVALID_TOKEN"',
                     "[00:00:04]: No auth token could be found."):
            self.assertEqual(explain(1, [line])[0]["key"], "needs_signin", line)

title: Crash help: the game needs Steam running

must_contain.why: a test for the new entry

instruction:
Add ONE new entry to the PATTERNS list in core/diagnose.py, in the same 5-part form as the
others: (key, regex, title, fix, link).

- key: "needs_steam_client"
- where in the list: directly BEFORE the "steam_init" entry (that entry also matches "failed to initialize steam", and the first match wins)
- the regex (case is ignored) must match these console lines: 'FATAL  : Failed to initialize Steam. Probably Steam client is not running.' - match on the 'steam client is not running' part, not on 'failed to initialize steam'
- title (exactly): "This game needs Steam running on the PC"
- fix (exactly, split over lines like the other entries so no line is over 118 characters): "This game's server only works while the Steam app is open and signed in on this PC. Start Steam, then start the server again."
- link: None

Then add assertions at the END of test_explain_patterns_and_exit_codes in tests/test_engine.py (same style,
8 spaces of indentation):
        f = explain(1, ["FATAL  : Failed to initialize Steam. Probably Steam client is not running."])
        self.assertEqual(f[0]["key"], "needs_steam_client")
        self.assertEqual(explain(1, ["SteamAPI_Init() failed"])[0]["key"], "steam_init")   # the general one still works

title: Crash help: Source game folder not given

must_contain.why: a test for the new entry

instruction:
Add ONE new entry to the PATTERNS list in core/diagnose.py, in the same 5-part form as the
others: (key, regex, title, fix, link).

- key: "source_game_folder"
- where in the list: directly BEFORE the "missing_install" entry
- the regex (case is ignored) must match these console lines: 'Unable to find gameinfo.txt. Solutions:'
- title (exactly): "The server wasn't told which game folder to use"
- fix (exactly, split over lines like the other entries so no line is over 118 characters): "This is a Source engine game. In Edit Server, add -game followed by the name of the folder that has gameinfo.txt in it to the launch options (for example -game cstrike), then start it again."
- link: None

Then add assertions at the END of test_explain_patterns_and_exit_codes in tests/test_engine.py (same style,
8 spaces of indentation):
        f = explain(1, ["Unable to find gameinfo.txt. Solutions:"])
        self.assertEqual(f[0]["key"], "source_game_folder")
        self.assertIn("-game", f[0]["fix"])

title: Crash help: one of the game's own files won't load

must_contain.why: a test for the new entry

instruction:
Add ONE new entry to the PATTERNS list in core/diagnose.py, in the same 5-part form as the
others: (key, regex, title, fix, link).

- key: "game_library"
- where in the list: directly AFTER the "vcredist_missing" entry (Microsoft's own DLLs must still be reported as vcredist_missing, which comes first)
- the regex (case is ignored) must match these console lines: 'src\public\tier1\interface.h (273) : Assertion Failed: Failed to load "SDL3.dll"' and 'Could not load library steam_api64.dll'
- title (exactly): "One of the game's own files couldn't be loaded"
- fix (exactly, split over lines like the other entries so no line is over 118 characters): "Use Install / repair to re-check the game files. If it keeps happening, this server may need to be started from a different folder or program - check the game's server guide."
- link: None

Then add assertions at the END of test_explain_patterns_and_exit_codes in tests/test_engine.py (same style,
8 spaces of indentation):
        f = explain(1, ['src\\public\\tier1\\interface.h (273) : Assertion Failed: Failed to load "SDL3.dll"'])
        self.assertEqual(f[0]["key"], "game_library")
        self.assertEqual(explain(1, ["Could not load library steam_api64.dll"])[0]["key"], "game_library")
        self.assertEqual(explain(1, ["Failed to load vcruntime140.dll"])[0]["key"], "vcredist_missing")

title: Closed-window errors: use later() in ark_window.py

excerpts.around: app\.after\(0, lambda: done\(res, err\) if win\.winfo_exists\(\) else None\)

must_not_contain.regex: app\.after\(0, lambda: done\(res, err\) if win\.winfo_exists\(\) else None\)
must_not_contain.why: this call must go through later()

instruction:
Background threads in this file hand their result to the window with `X.after(0, fn)`. When the
window has been closed (or BaoBun is closing) that raises "main thread is not in main loop" inside the thread.
There is a helper for exactly this in ui/app_common.py:

    def later(widget, fn):   # runs fn on the window's own thread; does nothing if the window is gone

Do exactly this and nothing else:
1. Add the line `from ui.app_common import later` directly after the line `import customtkinter as ctk`.
2. In the `work()` functions shown, change each `X.after(0, SOMETHING)` into `later(X, SOMETHING)` - same X, same
   SOMETHING, same indentation. There is 1 call to change (shown in the excerpts).

title: Game list: three games need a Steam account
checks: from core.game_catalog import GAME_PRESETS as G; import sys; bad=[n for n in ['Serious Sam HD: The Second Encounter', 'Takedown: Red Sabre', 'Eden Star'] if G[n].get('anonymous_login') is not False]; print('still anonymous:', bad); sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
from core.game_catalog import GAME_PRESETS as G; import sys; n=sum(1 for v in G.values() if v.get('anonymous_login') is False); print(n); sys.exit(0 if n < 60 else 1)
instruction:
The smoke test showed that Steam refuses to give these three games' server files without a Steam account
that owns the game. In presets.json, change "anonymous_login": true to "anonymous_login": false for exactly these
three games and no others: Serious Sam HD: The Second Encounter, Takedown: Red Sabre, Eden Star.

"anonymous_login": true appears for many games, so each SEARCH part must start at the game's "name" line and
run down to its "anonymous_login" line so that it matches only that game. Change nothing else.

instruction:
`rel_or_abs(base, path)` in core/mods_common.py has no tests. Create the NEW file tests/test_local_rel_or_abs.py (empty SEARCH part) with a unittest.TestCase that
tests it: at least 6 assertions, covering the normal cases and the edge cases you can see in the code.

don't guess. Use os.path.join / tempfile for paths so the test works on any PC; never write a drive letter you don't build with os.path.
